about: The build's task tree, derived from books/target by tools/plan-tasks.ts (docs/design/swarm.md, section 5). Do not edit: change the book or the script, then regenerate. It holds no counts over the book, so lanes that change different tasks never conflict here.

tasks.title: Capxul rebuilt
tasks.goal: Capxul runs on the new stack and does everything the built book's operations promise (the old 215 less what the cut classified, plus the plugs and the door): every eval passes at the head of integration/build on a devnet, the system evals and the size budget hold, and staging's live evals hold for a week.

exit.claim: Aaron accepts the rebuild.

tasks.title: B0 Spike: durable execution
tasks.goal: Effect Workflow and Cluster on Postgres are proven for the book's processes, or a decision chooses the fallback (DBOS on Postgres) and the book follows it.

tasks.title: B1 Generators
tasks.goal: packages/generate regenerates every src/generated/ folder from the records with no diff, every package compiles, and the migrations apply to an empty Postgres.

tasks.title: B2 Eval harness
tasks.goal: packages/evals, within 2,000 lines, lists the catalogue and runs any eval by id on a devnet world through the real CLI, as swarmD's runner contract says.

tasks.title: B3 Spine and pilots
tasks.goal: The devnet and the runtime run, the pilots (sign in, set up an Account, send a payment) pass every eval within budget, and each concept's line budget is set from what they measure.

tasks.title: B4 Concepts on the critical path
tasks.goal: Every concept's lane is done: each operation the built book keeps (the old 215 less what the cut classified: Frappe's, dropped or parked) has every eval of its record, and of every record under it, passing at the head of integration/build.

tasks.title: B5 New staging
tasks.goal: The new staging runs the same suite, and its live evals hold for a week.

tasks.title: D0 The portal
tasks.goal: The portal (docs/design/portal.md) is live behind Access: a page for every record, Review with typed answers, the stands, the scoreboard and the CLI surface, with Markdown and JSON twins.

tasks.title: T0 Tooling
tasks.goal: The pinned toolchain, one strict lint standard with Capxul's own rules, the formatter, the hooks, CI and the few cross-file checks, exactly as docs/design/tooling.md gives them, before any product code.

tasks.title: B0 Resume, signal and timer
tasks.goal: A process killed mid-run resumes, a signal resumes a waiting instance, and a timer fires, on the throwaway Postgres.

exit.claim: A process killed mid-run resumes on Effect Workflow and Cluster over Postgres.
A signal resumes a waiting instance.
A timer fires.

tasks.title: B0 An activity's side effect lands once
tasks.goal: An activity retried after a crash has its side effect land exactly once, through an idempotency key or a claim-before-call row, as the book's design does.

exit.claim: An activity retried after a crash has its side effect land once.

tasks.title: B0 Wake routing by keys, and the decisions
tasks.goal: A chain event and a withdraw transition, routed by their keys, wake the same waiting instance, and the runtime's choices are decision records.

exit.claim: A chain event and a withdraw transition, routed by their routing keys, reach the same waiting instance.
How the runtime learns of a new indexed row and where the key-to-instance map lives are decision records; or a decision chooses DBOS and the book is updated.

tasks.title: B1 Counterparty admissions, book first
tasks.goal: The read-only admissions counterparties need on company rows are in the book (rules.counterparty-reads) before the policies are generated.

exit.claim: Every rpc whose who is a counterparty reads company rows only through a read-only admission clause in the book.

tasks.title: B1 Telemetry and eval catalogues
tasks.goal: The telemetry catalogue (one event per machine, plus the runtime spans) and the eval catalogue are generated.

exit.claim: The generated telemetry and eval catalogues equal the book's machines, spans and evals.

tasks.title: B1 Regenerate with no diff

exit.claim: pnpm exec tsc -b compiles every package.

tasks.title: B1 Migrations and schemas

tasks.title: B2 The runner contract
tasks.goal: `eval list --json` and `eval run --json --out <dir> -- <ids>` print exactly the catalogue and one RunResult per id.

tasks.title: B2 Worlds as devnet snapshots
tasks.goal: The world builder builds each world a refusal or claim names from its steps, as the devnet concept designs it, and restores it as a named snapshot once the operations its steps run exist.

exit.claim: The world builder builds a world from its steps and restores it by name, and lists every world whose steps run an operation not built yet, with those operations, as not yet buildable.

tasks.title: B3 The pilots pass
tasks.goal: Sign in, set up an Account and send a payment, and the devnet commands the world builder runs, pass every eval of their tasks at the integration head that a buildable world allows, within budget.

exit.claim: In one run at the integration head, every eval of the pilot closure passes within its budget, except those whose world's steps run an operation not built yet, which read unverifiable and name that world.

tasks.title: B3 The devnet in a swarmD sandbox, and the gate's scope
tasks.goal: A swarmD sandbox boots the devnet from a golden snapshot and runs an L1 eval fast enough for pairs, otherwise a decision records the fallback host; and the gate refuses a change outside the task's paths.

exit.claim: At an integration head newer than its golden snapshot, the devnet boots in a swarmD sandbox in at most 2 minutes and one L1 eval runs in at most 10 seconds, or a decision records the fallback: one long-lived devnet host, a world restored per pair under a lock.

With SWARMD_TASK_PATHS set, the project's gate fails on a change outside the task's paths, or to packages/book or packages/evals from a lane task, and admits the regenerated outputs only when generate:check and plan-tasks --check pass.

tasks.title: B3 A shared world
tasks.goal: The devnet stack runs as a shared world behind its world gateway over HTTPS, in seasons (aaron.seasons, devnet.seasons): the owner's grant controls the clock and plans each season, which starts from a saved world, runs at its rate, warps on a real schedule and ends in a reset; joiners reach it with their own grants only while a season they play runs, and nothing leaves it (devnet.season-players).

exit.claim: A shared world boots on one host and passes its smoke journey; a joiner's grant reads its own mail while a season they play runs and is refused ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED when it moves the clock.
A season created, started, warped on its schedule and ended on one shared world leaves `<name>-end` saved and the reset world restored, and a player's next call after the reset is NOT_AUTHENTICATED.

tasks.title: auth list: List signed-in people
tasks.goal: `capxul auth list` does what operation auth.list promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the people signed in on this machine and marks the current one. Each row says whether the person is a human or an AI that signs with its own key. Use it to see who you can switch to.

tasks.title: auth logout: Sign out
tasks.goal: `capxul auth logout` does what operation auth.logout promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Signs a person out on this device. Without `--email` it signs out the current person. It removes the session here first and then asks the backend to revoke it.

tasks.title: auth switch: Switch person
tasks.goal: `capxul auth switch` does what operation auth.switch promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Makes another person who is already signed in on this machine the current one. At a terminal you can leave out the email and pick from a list, which also offers to sign in someone else. The CLI checks the session with the backend before it switches.

tasks.title: config telemetry off: Turn telemetry off
tasks.goal: `capxul config telemetry off` does what operation config.telemetry.off promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Turns off usage and diagnostics collection for this CLI. It saves the preference and reports the resulting status.

tasks.title: config telemetry on: Turn telemetry on
tasks.goal: `capxul config telemetry on` does what operation config.telemetry.on promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Turns on usage and diagnostics collection for this CLI. It saves the preference and reports the resulting status.

tasks.title: config telemetry status: Telemetry status
tasks.goal: `capxul config telemetry status` does what operation config.telemetry.status promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows whether this CLI collects usage and diagnostics. It also says when this build has no place to send them, or when an environment variable forces collection off.

tasks.title: schema: Read the command schema
tasks.goal: `capxul schema` does what operation schema promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Prints the CLI's own description as JSON. With no words it lists every command, whether it moves money, the global flags and the exit codes. With a command, such as `capxul schema payment send`, it gives that command's arguments, flags, output and error codes. Agents use it to look up a command instead of guessing flags.

tasks.title: use env: Choose an environment
tasks.goal: `capxul use env` does what operation use.env promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Saves the environment later commands use: devnet, staging, beta or production. The CLI has no built-in default, so you choose one before the first command that needs the network.

tasks.title: use personal: Act as yourself
tasks.goal: `capxul use personal` does what operation use.personal promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Makes later commands act for you yourself instead of an Organization. Use it after `capxul use org` to go back to your own account.

tasks.title: whoami: Who am I
tasks.goal: `capxul whoami` does what operation whoami promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows who you are, who you act as, the Safe and the environment. It reads only files on this machine, so it answers fast and makes no network call. With `--json` it also says where each value came from.

tasks.title: auth login: Sign in

With `--own-key` it sets up an AI's own account, which signs with its own key.

tasks.title: auth verify: Finish signing in

Scripts and agents use it as the second of two sign-in commands.

tasks.title: account show: Show your account

tasks.title: dev fund: Fund with test money

tasks.title: referral invite: Invite someone to the beta

tasks.title: referral list: List the people you referred
tasks.goal: `capxul referral list` does what operation referral.list promises: its 1 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the people you referred, with each one's email masked, how they came and their stage.

tasks.title: referral: Show your referral link
tasks.goal: `capxul referral` does what operation referral.show promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows your referral link, how many invites you have left and how many people you referred reached each stage. Your first look makes your code.

tasks.title: waitlist invites grant: Give someone more invites
tasks.goal: `capxul waitlist invites grant` does what operation waitlist.invites.grant promises: its 0 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Not written in the old book.

tasks.title: waitlist join: Join the beta waitlist
tasks.goal: `capxul waitlist join` does what operation waitlist.join promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. tasks.title: waitlist status: Check the beta waitlist
tasks.goal: `capxul waitlist status` does what operation waitlist.status promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows whether Capxul has let you into the beta. It says `admitted` with the date, `open` when the beta needs no admission, or `waiting`. For `waiting` it also shows the date you joined and what you said you will build.

tasks.title: org head app add: Add a Frappe app the Organization needs
tasks.goal: `capxul org head app add` does what operation org.head.app.add promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Asks for a Frappe app beyond the fundamental ones, such as Helpdesk: one Capxul can ask a head's host to install. It lives only on a connected head, so with no head it waits, wanted; with a head on Frappe Cloud, its host is asked to install it, and on a self-hosted head its owner installs it with bench; either way it is listed installed once the head shows it. Adding an app already wanted, or installed on the head, changes nothing; a fundamental app is always installed and is refused. A Director runs it, or the Organization's FDE for a Director who asks it in conversation.

tasks.title: org head app list: List the Organization's Frappe apps
tasks.goal: `capxul org head app list` does what operation org.head.app.list promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the Frappe apps the Organization runs: the fundamental ones (Frappe, ERPNext's accounting and projects, Frappe HR's payroll, Frappe CRM), held natively by Capxul from the first day, head or no head; and every other app it asked for, which lives only on a connected head: wanted until the head installs it, installed with the version the head runs, or removed. Use it to see what the FDE or a Director added, and what a head still has to install.

tasks.title: invite decline: Decline an invitation
tasks.goal: `capxul invite decline` does what operation invite.decline promises: its 5 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Declines an invitation sent to you. The offer ends, and anything it had set up on the chain is cleaned up. Only you can decline your own offer.

tasks.title: invite list: List your invitations
tasks.goal: `capxul invite list` does what operation invite.list promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the invitations sent to you, from any Organization. Each one shows its Organization, phase, expiry and offered grants. Use it to find the invitation ID for `invite accept`. With `--json`, each invitation also carries its offer digest.

tasks.title: org create: Create an Organization
tasks.goal: `capxul org create` does what operation org.create promises: its 7 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Creates one Organization from a name, a `--handle` and a two-letter `--country`, then follows its setup until it is ready. You sign the founder authorization in your browser. If this machine already recorded a create for the same handle, the command picks up that Organization instead of making a second one.

tasks.title: org fde ask: Ask the Organization's hosted FDE something
tasks.goal: `capxul org fde ask` does what operation org.fde.ask promises: its 7 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Sends a message to the Organization's Forward Deployed Engineer on Capxul's host, and prints its reply when its turn ends. Any member may ask, and so may a guest the Organization's management named. The FDE then works as the asker: it does for them only what their own hats allow, and anything that needs a signature comes to the asker to approve. At the deadline (`--timeout-seconds`, 300 by default) the command stops waiting and prints the turn's id (`org fde turn get` reads it later), and the FDE carries on. A guest names the Organization with `--org`. A paused FDE takes no message until its hosting is paid (`org fde pay`).

tasks.title: org fde guest add: Let an outside person the Organization works with talk to it…
tasks.goal: `capxul org fde guest add` does what operation org.fde.guest.add promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Names someone outside the Organization whom it works with (a customer, a supplier, an accountant, someone it may hire) as a guest who may talk to its hosted FDE, by email or a person's @handle, with an optional note of who they are. A guest holds no Seat and no hat, so the FDE does for them only what they may do themselves: see their own dealings with the Organization, never its members' records. Someone not yet on Capxul is admitted so they can sign in, and is told how to ask. Naming someone twice changes nothing.

tasks.title: org fde guest list: List the outside people who may talk to the Organization's …
tasks.goal: `capxul org fde guest list` does what operation org.fde.guest.list promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the Organization's guests, the active ones first (newest named first), then the removed ones, or only one kind with `--status active|removed`: each with who they are, the note, who named them and when, and when they were removed. Paged with `--limit` and `--after`.

tasks.title: org fde guest remove: Stop an outside person talking to the Organization's FDE
tasks.goal: `capxul org fde guest remove` does what operation org.fde.guest.remove promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Removes a guest: from then on they may not ask the FDE, and the FDE no longer acts for them on anything they asked before. Their past asks stay recorded. Naming them again lets them ask again.

tasks.title: org fde show: Show the Organization's hosted FDE and what its hosting costs
tasks.goal: `capxul org fde show` does what operation org.fde.show promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows the Organization's Forward Deployed Engineer, which Capxul hosts: its handle and Safe, whether it is running, due, paused or resuming on the host, the hats its Safe wears (it acts with each asker's, not these), the instant its hosting is paid to and the day it falls due, the price of a month (FDE_HOSTING_PRICE), what has been paid, and who last asked it something. Null for an Organization started without one.

tasks.title: org fde turn get: Read one of your turns with the hosted FDE, and its reply
tasks.goal: `capxul org fde turn get` does what operation org.fde.turn.get promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Reads a turn the hosted FDE took for a message you sent: still working, ended with its reply, or failed with the host's reason. Use it after `org fde ask` stopped waiting at its deadline. Only the asker reads a turn: the reply may hold what only they may see.

tasks.title: org head app remove: Stop wanting a Frappe app
tasks.goal: `capxul org head app remove` does what operation org.head.app.remove promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Stops wanting an app the Organization added, so Capxul no longer asks a head's host to install it; it stays listed as removed. The head's owner uninstalls it on the head, and Capxul deletes none of the head's documents. A fundamental app is never removed. Adding it again wants it again.

tasks.title: org head connect: Connect a Frappe site as the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head connect` does what operation org.head.connect promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 7 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Connects a Frappe site, on Frappe Cloud or self-hosted, as the Organization's head: once connected, accounting, payroll, the CRM and projects sync with it, and Capxul stays the record of money and identity. It reads the head user's API key and secret, and on Frappe Cloud the team's token, from a prompt or from `--key-file` and `--team-token-file`, never from a flag; previews what connecting shares and asks (`--confirm` answers yes in a script); then follows the site's check until the head is connected, or failing with the reason. An Organization has at most one live head.

tasks.title: org head disconnect: Disconnect the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head disconnect` does what operation org.head.disconnect promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. After a preview, disconnects the Organization's live head: every sync stops, Capxul keeps every record it holds and the head keeps its own documents. The head's key is never used again, and its later rings are refused. A new connection can be made afterwards.

tasks.title: org head doc-call list: List the document family's calls to the head: who, what…
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc-call list` does what operation org.head.doc-call.list promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the calls `org head doc` and `org head doctype` made to the head, newest first: whose authority each ran with (a member's, or the FDE's for the member who asked it), the head User, what it did to which document, and whether it was done or refused and why; never a field's value. A Director sees every call; any other member sees the calls made with their own authority. `--doctype`, `--name` and, for a Director, `--member` narrow it.

tasks.title: org head doc amend: Amend a cancelled document on the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc amend` does what operation org.head.doc.amend promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 9 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Makes the correction of a cancelled head document, as Frappe's Amend does: a new draft copied from it, whose `amended_from` names it and whose name, by Frappe's default, is the old one with `-1` (an amendment's amendment `-2`). Change and submit the draft as any other.

tasks.title: org head doc apply: Take a Workflow action on a document on the Organization's …
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc apply` does what operation org.head.doc.apply promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 9 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Takes one action of the Workflow a head DocType runs under (such as Shortlist or Reject on a Job Applicant), as your own User there: the document moves to the action's next state, submitting or cancelling it when that state says so. `org head doc get` lists the actions you may take.

tasks.title: org head doc cancel: Cancel a submitted document on the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc cancel` does what operation org.head.doc.cancel promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 9 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Cancels a submitted head document, as Frappe's Cancel does: it is kept, cancelled for good, and `org head doc amend` makes its correction. A document that submitted documents still link to cannot be cancelled until they are, and one under a Workflow moves only by `org head doc apply`.

tasks.title: org head doc change: Change a document on the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc change` does what operation org.head.doc.change promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 9 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Changes a head document's fields with `--set`, `--file` or `--clear <field>` (repeatable; as create takes them, a `--set` over the file's field and a field both set and cleared CLI_USAGE), keeping the rest. Its status never changes here: `org head doc submit`, `cancel` and `apply` do that. A submitted document takes only the fields its DocType lets change after submission. `--modified <stamp>`, from `org head doc get`, refuses the change if someone changed the document since.

tasks.title: org head doc create: Create a document on the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc create` does what operation org.head.doc.create promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 8 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Creates a document of a DocType that lives only on the head, as your own User there, with `--set <field>=<value>` (repeatable; the value sent as text, for the head to read as its field's type) and `--file <path>` (a JSON object of fields with their types, child tables as arrays of rows); with both, each `--set` overrides the file's field of that name. The head names it, fills its defaults and runs its own checks; a submittable one is made a draft. It is the head's document: Capxul keeps no copy of it, only the call in its log.

tasks.title: org head doc get: Show one document on the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc get` does what operation org.head.doc.get promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 7 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows one head document by its DocType and its name on the head: every field your head User may read, its child rows, whether it is a draft, submitted or cancelled, its Workflow state and the actions you may take, and what you may do to it (change, submit, cancel, amend, remove). `--field` (repeatable) prints only those fields.

tasks.title: org head doc list: List documents of a DocType on the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc list` does what operation org.head.doc.list promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 7 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the documents of one DocType that lives only on the connected head, such as `Job Opening` or `Appraisal`, as your own User on the head may see them: newest change first, with each one's name, status and list fields. `--filter <field><op><value>` (repeatable, all applying together; the operator is the longest of `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `~` like and `!~` not like after the field's name, and `%` in the value is like's wildcard), `--field` (repeatable) and `--order-by` shape it. What a native concept holds (projects, the CRM, payroll and HR's leave and expenses, the books) has its own commands, and money is never read here.

tasks.title: org head doc remove: Delete a document on the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc remove` does what operation org.head.doc.remove promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 12 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Deletes a head document that is not submitted (a draft, a cancelled one, or one of a DocType that is never submitted), as Frappe's Delete does, after a preview, since it cannot be undone from Capxul; `--confirm` answers yes in a script. A submitted document is cancelled, never deleted.

tasks.title: org head doc submit: Submit a draft document on the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doc submit` does what operation org.head.doc.submit promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 9 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Submits a draft of a submittable DocType on the head, such as a Training Event or an Appraisal, as your own User there: it becomes submitted and its fields are fixed, as Frappe's Submit does. A DocType under a Workflow moves by `org head doc apply` instead.

tasks.title: org head doctype get: Show one of the head's DocTypes: its fields, Workflow and…
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doctype get` does what operation org.head.doctype.get promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows one DocType on the connected head: its fields and child tables with their types and which are mandatory, whether it is submitted, its Workflow's states and actions, what your head User may do with it, and whether `org head doc` reaches it or which commands do. Use it to know what `org head doc create --set` takes.

tasks.title: org head doctype list: List the head's DocTypes that the document family reaches
tasks.goal: `capxul org head doctype list` does what operation org.head.doctype.list promises: its 5 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the DocTypes of the apps on the connected head that `org head doc` reaches, by name, with each one's app and module and whether it is submitted. `--all` lists every other one too, with why it is not reached: a native one names the commands that reach it, a money one is Capxul's, and the head's machinery is never reached. `--app` and `--module` narrow it.

tasks.title: org head show: Show the Organization's head
tasks.goal: `capxul org head show` does what operation org.head.show promises: its 5 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows the Organization's live head: its site and host, whether it is connecting, connected or failing and why, Frappe's and the Capxul app's versions, its time zone, who connected it, when it was last checked and last rang, and the Organization's apps as the head runs them. Null when there is none. It never shows a key or a token.

tasks.title: org invite cancel: Cancel an invitation
tasks.goal: `capxul org invite cancel` does what operation org.invite.cancel promises: its 5 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Cancels an invitation the Organization sent that has not been accepted. Any rights the offer had set up on the chain are then cleaned up. Use it when you invited the wrong person or offered the wrong grants.

tasks.title: org invite list: List sent invitations
tasks.goal: `capxul org invite list` does what operation org.invite.list promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the invitations the Organization has sent, with each one's phase, delivery, expiry and offered grants. Use `--phase` to narrow it, for example to pending offers.

tasks.title: org invite resend: Resend an invitation
tasks.goal: `capxul org invite resend` does what operation org.invite.resend promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Sends a pending invitation to its recipient again. Use it when someone says the first message never arrived. It never extends the offer's expiry.

tasks.title: org list: List your Organizations
tasks.goal: `capxul org list` does what operation org.list promises: its 5 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists the Organizations you can act in, with each one's handle, ID, setup state and account address. It also lists any Organization setups you started that are not finished. Use it to find the handle or ID that other commands take.

tasks.title: org me: Your standing
tasks.goal: `capxul org me` does what operation org.me promises: its 6 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows your standing in the Organization: your role, whether you can manage people or spend, whether you are a Director, how many approvals changes need, your assignments and the spending allowances you can pay from. Use it to see what you are allowed to do before you try.

tasks.title: org member get: Show a Seat
tasks.goal: `capxul org member get` does what operation org.member.get promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Adds one contact to the address book of whoever you act as. You name them by handle, email, wallet address or PartyId, with an optional label. At a terminal it asks for each field, and in a script you pass the JSON with `--input`.

tasks.title: contact change: Change what a book keeps about one entry
tasks.goal: `capxul contact change` does what operation contact.change promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Changes the details your book, or with `--org` the Organization's, keeps about one entry, named by its id as `contact list` prints it: a person's mailboxes, numbers, job title and company, or a company's website, industry, territory, size, annual revenue and description. Each detail given replaces the stored one, `--clear` empties one, and the rest stay. `--email` and `--phone`, when given, replace the whole list, the first primary. The entry keeps its id, its label (`contact label` changes it) and its Party: a mailbox given to a private person is only a detail, and only `contact link` decides where money paid to the entry goes. A change that gives nothing is refused.

tasks.title: contact hide: Hide a contact

Hides one contact from your address book list. The contact is not deleted. You can still read it with `contact get` or see it with `contact list --include-hidden`.

tasks.title: contact label: Rename a contact
tasks.goal: `capxul contact label` does what operation contact.label promises: its 3 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Changes the label shown for one contact. You name the contact by PartyId, or pick one at a terminal.

tasks.title: contact link: Name the Party a private entry is, once
tasks.goal: `capxul contact link` does what operation contact.link promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Names the Party a private entry of your book, or with `--org` the Organization's, is: a person by their mailbox, @handle, address or Party id; a company by its Organization's @handle, its address or its Party id. From then on money paid to the entry reaches that Party, and the entry keeps its id. It cannot be undone, so at a terminal it shows the entry and what it will be linked to and asks; `--confirm` answers yes from a script. An entry that already has a Party, a Party already in the book, and a Party of the other kind are refused.

tasks.title: agent create: Create an agent
tasks.goal: `capxul agent create` does what operation agent.create promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 6 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Gives an agent an account of its own, with you as its owner. The CLI makes the agent's key on this machine and sends only its address. You approve one call from your Safe, which deploys the agent's Safe (Safe 1.5.0) with that key as its one signer and enables the AgentOwner module, so your Safe can freeze it, replace its key, sweep it and remove it. AgentOwner is also the Safe's transaction guard and module guard, so the agent's own key can never call its Safe or delegatecall, and so it cannot switch your control off. The agent is then found by its `@handle`.

tasks.title: agent freeze: Freeze an agent
tasks.goal: `capxul agent freeze` does what operation agent.freeze promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Stops an agent's key from signing anything, at once. You approve one call from your Safe to `AgentOwner.freeze(safe)`, which swaps the key out of the agent's Safe for AgentOwner. Its Safe and what it holds stay as they are, and AgentOwner keeps the key so `agent unfreeze` can put it back.

tasks.title: agent key rotate: Replace an agent's key
tasks.goal: `capxul agent key rotate` does what operation agent.key.rotate promises: its 6 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Gives an active agent a new key and retires the old one. Your machine makes the new key and sends only its address. You approve one call from your Safe to `AgentOwner.swapSigner(safe, oldKey, newKey)`, which swaps the one owner of the agent's Safe for the new key. AgentOwner stays its module, transaction guard and module guard, and no other owner is added. Once it lands, the old key signs nothing for the agent, as a Safe transaction or as a user operation.

tasks.title: agent list: List your agents
tasks.goal: `capxul agent list` does what operation agent.list promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists every agent you own, newest first, with its handle, state and Safe. It reads the rows as they stand; `agent show` reads one agent from the chain.

tasks.title: agent remove: Remove an agent
tasks.goal: `capxul agent remove` does what operation agent.remove promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Ends an agent for good. You approve one call from your Safe to `AgentOwner.remove(safe, tokens)`, which sweeps every settlement asset the agent's Safe holds to your Safe and leaves AgentOwner as its one owner, so no key can sign for it again. Its handle stays taken. There is no undo.

tasks.title: agent show: Show an agent
tasks.goal: `capxul agent show` does what operation agent.show promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Reads one agent you own, by its `@handle` or its id. It shows its Account, the key it signs with, whether it is active, and what its Safe holds in each settlement asset, read from the chain. A create that was sent is settled from its receipt first.

tasks.title: agent sweep: Sweep an agent's Safe
tasks.goal: `capxul agent sweep` does what operation agent.sweep promises: its 6 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Moves all held settlement assets from an agent's Safe to you, or to a recipient you name. You approve one operation from your Safe, with one `AgentOwner.sweep(safe, to, token)` call per asset. Its key and Seats stay unchanged, and a frozen agent can be swept too.

tasks.title: agent unfreeze: Unfreeze an agent
tasks.goal: `capxul agent unfreeze` does what operation agent.unfreeze promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lets a frozen agent's key sign again. You approve one call from your Safe to `AgentOwner.unfreeze(safe)`, which puts the key back as the one owner of the agent's Safe.

tasks.title: dev season cancel: Cancel a planned season
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season cancel` does what operation dev.season.cancel promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Takes back a planned season before it starts, as `payment cancel` takes back a scheduled payment: its start and its warps never run, its name is not used again, and nothing in the world changes. A running season is ended with `dev season end` instead, which resets the world, so a script that meant to drop a season that has since started is refused rather than resetting it.

tasks.title: dev season change: Change a season's start, end, rate or reset
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season change` does what operation dev.season.change promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 5 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Changes a season's own fields: a planned season's start, end, rate and reset, and a running season's end and reset (a running season's clock takes its rate from `dev time set`). Its warps and players have their own commands. Nothing in the world moves now: a new end moves when the season ends and resets, a new start when it starts, and a new reset the world it resets to.

tasks.title: dev season create: Plan a season of the world
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season create` does what operation dev.season.create promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Plans a season, the way a shared world's time runs (aaron.seasons): the saved world it starts from, the rate its clock runs at, the real time it ends and, if given, the real time it starts itself, the warps that move its world on a schedule of real times, the people who play it, and the world its end resets to (its own starting world unless another is named, typically the next season's). Like a game, it starts from a known world, runs at a rate, jumps on a schedule and ends in a reset. Nothing in the world moves until it starts.

tasks.title: dev season end: End a season now and reset the world
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season end` does what operation dev.season.end promises: its 4 acceptance claims and 7 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Ends a running season now, as its scheduled end would. Its world is kept as its last state, the saved world `<name>-end`, and the world is reset to the season's reset world, frozen at that world's now, until the next season starts. Its players are refused until a season they play runs; then they sign in again, and their money, mail and everything they made are what that season's world holds. Only a running season ends: a planned one is taken back with `dev season cancel`, so `end` always resets the world. It previews what it ends and asks.

tasks.title: dev season list: List the world's seasons
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season list` does what operation dev.season.list promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 2 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Lists every season the world has had, a page at a time: the running one, the planned ones in the order they start, then the ended and cancelled ones, newest first, each with its starting and reset worlds, rate, window, players, warps (each with what it did) and the world its end kept. Anyone in the world may read it.

tasks.title: dev season player add: Let a person play a season
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season player add` does what operation dev.season.player.add promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Adds a person who holds a world grant to a season's players. While the season runs, the world's gateway admits them at once; they act as themselves, with their own dev signer, as anyone does in the world. A local devnet has no grants, so no players: everyone on the machine is its owner.

tasks.title: dev season player remove: Stop a person playing a season
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season player remove` does what operation dev.season.player.remove promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 4 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Takes a person out of a season's players. While the season runs, the world's gateway refuses their next call; what they made in the world stays in it, and their world grant stays for the seasons they still play.

tasks.title: dev season show: Show the world's current season
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season show` does what operation dev.season.show promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 1 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Shows the world's current season (the one running, else the next planned, else the last ended), whether you play it, its next scheduled warp and the clock. Anyone in the world may read it, between seasons too: it is how a player learns when the next season starts and when the world next jumps.

tasks.title: dev season start: Start a season now
tasks.goal: `capxul dev season start` does what operation dev.season.start promises: its 2 acceptance claims and 6 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. Starts a planned season now, as its scheduled start would: the world becomes its starting world, at that world's now under a new world epoch, and its clock runs at the season's rate until the season ends, jumping at each of its scheduled warps. Its players may act in it from then on, and they are the only joiners who may. Whatever the world held before is replaced, so it previews what it replaces and asks.

tasks.title: dev season warp add: Schedule a warp in a season

At its time the world's supervisor runs it as `dev time warp` does: a barrier that stops at every due instant on the way, so a month's dated payments, notices and closes happen on their own days. While it runs, players' calls are refused and the clock and season reads answer. A warp in a planned season runs only once the season runs.

tasks.title: dev time set: Set how fast the devnet's clock runs
tasks.goal: `capxul dev time set` does what operation dev.time.set promises: its 5 acceptance claims and 3 refusals hold, its --json shape, events, spans and budget pass on a devnet at the head of integration/build, and its reference page agrees with it. A frozen clock stays frozen and runs at the rate when it resumes. Warps are unchanged: a warp moves the clock as far as it is told, whatever the rate.
